abstract: Maintains shallow water bathymetry charts and safe under-keel navigation clearance data
system_message:
You are Hydrographic authority safety inspector (HYDR). The Hydrographic authority safety inspector (HYDR) oversees shallow water bathymetry charts and safe under-keel navigation clearance data, and provides operational tidal stream velocity telemetry for maritime emergency salvage corridors.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains shallow water bathymetry charts and safe under-keel navigation clearance data（CHNL）
information_points.content:
HYDR-CHNL-7HP：For the Dynamic Deflection and Deep Skimming Array, bathymetric transit assessments along the towage corridor between the incident reef and the sheltered bay indicate an under-keel navigation clearance of 4.8 m, measured as the minimum vertical separation between the vessel's deepest draft point and the seabed at lowest astronomical tide.
HYDR-CHNL-JCN：For Perimeter Boom Containment and Subsea Inerting, bathymetric calculations along the towage corridor between the incident reef and the sheltered bay establish an under-keel navigation clearance of 4.2 m, reflecting the minimum vertical separation between the vessel's deepest draft point and the seabed at lowest astronomical tide.
HYDR-CHNL-CEQ：For Controlled Hull Girdling and Direct Pumping, transit calculations along the towage corridor between the incident reef and the sheltered bay document an under-keel navigation clearance of 3.2 m at lowest astronomical tide between the vessel's deepest draft point and the seabed.

information_points.title: Tidal stream velocity telemetry（TIDE）
information_points.content:
HYDR-TIDE-HHA：Modeled hydrographic data for the emergency containment fairway indicates that the peak spring ebb current for Perimeter Boom Containment and Subsea Inerting is 2.6 m/s at the maximum surface current velocity during spring ebb tide.
HYDR-TIDE-66K：According to the hydrographic tidal survey within the emergency containment fairway, the peak spring ebb current for Controlled Hull Girdling and Direct Pumping reaches 3.4 m/s at maximum modeled surface velocity during spring ebb tide.
HYDR-TIDE-O2M：Hydrographic tidal survey data for the emergency containment fairway indicates that the peak spring ebb current for the Dynamic Deflection and Deep Skimming Array is 1.8 m/s, representing the maximum modeled surface current velocity during spring ebb tide.
